messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: directed derivatives with stan-math
parts:
Hi!

Does stan-math offer a facility to calculate a directed derivative of a vector-valued function f?

Or is it best to simply calculate the Jacobian and multiply this with the direction I am interested in?

Also: If there is a directed derivative available - how does this compare performance wise wrt to taking the Jacobian and then multiplying the vector?

Many thanks!

Best,
Sebastian

PS: this is a stan-math users question for sure, please move to stan-dev if more appropiate there.

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] directed derivatives with stan-math
parts:
Hi Sebastian,

You'll find a convenience function, gradient_dot_vector, located in stan/math/mix/mat/functor/gradient_dot_vector.hpp.

It uses forward mode to compute it, so it may not work for every expression in the math library.

We haven't done empirical comparisons for speed.


Daniel


P.S. putting it on the users list is the right place for this questions.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] directed derivatives with stan-math
parts:
It'll be a lot faster than reverse mode! No memory
allocation and no virtual function calls and at
most the same multiply-add operations for the chain
rule.

Having said that, the forward-mode code is hardly
optimal. It'd behoove us to take another pass through
it all, test it thoroughly, then go through yet
another pass and optimize.

- Bob
